summaryZh: 文章基于Bushel 2026年农场状况调查及行业访谈，指出AI在农业中的应用已跨越年龄界限，主要分化在农场规模；目前农户多用通用AI工具处理文档，未来AI有望整合数据孤岛、辅助农艺与经济决策，并像智能手机一样成为农场日常效率工具。文章还介绍了先正达等企业利用AI加速化合物研发的案例。
featuredReason: 文章虽以种植业为主要语境，但清晰揭示了AI在农业中跨越规模与年龄的采用规律、数据孤岛整合价值及企业级研发应用，对智慧畜牧从业者理解AI落地路径和农户心理具有跨品类参考意义。

Surprising ways AI may improve your farm

Large farms aren’t the only ones that will benefit from adopting artificial intelligence. AI can positively impact farms of all sizes.

Gil Gullickson,Editor,Wallaces FarmerOctober 28, 2026

schedule3 Min Read

Although it’s still early in the game, artificial intelligence has the potential to drive on-farm efficiencies to a level far above where they are now. JuSun/Getty Images

link

At a Glance

So far, farmers mainly use AI tools for writing and editing documents.

In the future, AI could play a role in better sorting data from which to make agronomic and economic decisions.

AI will change agriculture, just as smartphones have. 

Each November, the outlook issue of Wallaces Farmer — including this year’s “Smart Moves for 2027” package — contains some surprising developments.

This year, it’s artificial intelligence. It’s not so much the technology that’s an eye-opener; it’s also farmer interest.

You’d normally expect younger farmers to embrace AI more than older producers. That’s not happening, said Marc Rosenbohm, a senior grain and oilseeds analyst for Terrain.

An analysis by Rosenbohm — Bushels’ 2026 State of the Farm — shows that AI use spreads across all age groups. Instead, the split occurs in farm size. Those in the lower two-thirds of farm sizes — less than 5,000 acres — hesitate more to use AI than farmers with large farms.

“Concerns about time constraints exist,” Rosenbohm said. “There is also uncertainty about how it could benefit them.”

Rapid AI adoption

“This is a book that has yet to be written,” said Ryan Schaefer, vice president of New Holland North America.

Related:Smart drainage tech helps farmers control water table remotely

However, agricultural companies are rapidly using AI.

“We are leveraging AI to enhance machine technologies and data analytics to deliver value to farmers in terms of the quality of the crop as it's coming to the combine,” Schaefer said.

Syngenta uses AI to develop new chemical formulations.

“We are using AI to help anticipate what comes next,” said Jeff Cecil, president of North American crop protection for Syngenta. “We take products that we've formulated or developed to help us understand what worked and what didn’t. Then AI can help identify the most promising paths for the next wave of new formulations.”

Syngenta uses the same AI pattern to search for new chemical active ingredients.

“Using AI, we can quickly narrow 150,000-plus molecules down to 50,000 for further evaluation,” Cecil said. “We developed our very first completely AI-driven molecule and launched it in Brazil this last year.”

On the farm

Rosenbohm’s analysis found farmers mainly deploy general-use AI tools — such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot — more than agriculture-specific AI ones. Office-based tasks such as drafting or editing documents so far make up the main use of AI by farmers.

“Among mid-to-upper-sized farms, we’ve seen AI use venture into business and financial analysis,” Rosenbohm said. “We don't have good insights on how deep it goes, but they are experimenting with and using it.”

Rosenbohm said AI could potentially piece together data across various agricultural platforms.

“Some of the survey results showed that there may be some data silo issues occurring,” he said. “AI can help make connections to integrate those data insights.”

Related:How to avoid being hustled by AI slop

Schaefer noted that early adopters in agriculture use AI for tasks they normally would have directed off the farm, such as legal or business advice. He added a major future opportunity for farmers is using AI to match production volume with commodity market moves.

But benefits aren’t limited to large farms.

“You can drive efficiencies on every farm of every size through adoption of AI tools,” Schaefer said.

The way it works

If AI use seems far off, think of the smartphone that many of you have.

“If you rewind 10 or 15 years ago, we couldn’t have imagined having this supercomputer in our hands,” said Jim Knuth, senior vice president of Farm Credit Services of America. “You no longer have to print off a paper map. You don’t have to watch the 5 o’clock news to figure out what the weather's going to be. We have gotten so used to the way it works.”

Knuth sees the same trend occurring with AI in agriculture.

“I know some people will say, ‘Oh, it’s going to wreck the world,’” he said. “No. This is not stopping. In a few years, AI use will be common, just the way things work. It will be another way we can drive needed efficiency in our businesses.”

Related:Stressed by crop scouting? Plant sensors and robots may help

About the Author

Gil Gullickson

Editor, Wallaces Farmer

Gil Gullickson grew up on a farm that he now owns near Langford, S.D., and graduated with an agronomy degree from South Dakota State University. Earlier in his career, he spent 13 years as a Farm Progress editor, covering Minnesota and the Dakotas.

Gullickson is a widely respected and decorated ag journalist, earning the Agricultural Communicators Network writing award for Writer of the Year three times, and winning Story of the Year four times. He is a past winner of the International Federation of Agricultural Journalists’ Food and Agriculture Organization Award for Food Security. He has served as president of both ACN and the North American Agricultural Journalists.

translationZh:
尽管现在还处于早期阶段，人工智能有潜力将农场效率提升到远高于当前的水平。

**概览**

到目前为止，农民主要将AI工具用于撰写和编辑文档。

未来，AI可能在更好地整理数据方面发挥作用，从而帮助做出农艺和经济决策。

AI将改变农业，就像智能手机曾经做到的那样。

每年11月，《Wallaces Farmer》的展望特刊——包括今年的“2027年明智之举”专题——都会包含一些令人惊讶的动态。

今年，是人工智能。令人大开眼界的与其说是技术本身，不如说是农民的兴趣。

通常你会认为年轻农民比年长生产者更愿意接受AI。但事实并非如此，Terrain的高级谷物和油籽分析师Marc Rosenbohm说。

Rosenbohm的一项分析——Bushel的《2026年农场状况》——显示AI的使用跨越所有年龄组。相反，分化出现在农场规模上。农场规模处于后三分之二——即低于5000英亩——的农户比大型农场主更犹豫使用AI。

“存在对时间限制的担忧，”Rosenbohm说。“也有人不确定AI能给他们带来什么好处。”

**AI的快速采用**

“这是一本尚未写就的书，”New Holland北美副总裁Ryan Schaefer说。

然而，农业公司正在迅速使用AI。

“我们正在利用AI增强机器技术和数据分析，在作物进入联合收割机时为其质量向农民传递价值，”Schaefer说。

先正达利用AI开发新的化学配方。

“我们正在使用AI帮助预测下一步，”先正达北美作物保护总裁Jeff Cecil说。“我们拿已经配制或开发的产品，帮助自己理解哪些有效、哪些无效。然后AI可以帮助确定下一波新配方最有希望的路径。”

先正达使用相同的AI模式来搜索新的化学活性成分。

“使用AI，我们可以迅速将15万多种分子缩小到5万种进行进一步评估，”Cecil说。“我们开发了首个完全由AI驱动的分子，并于去年在巴西推出。”

**在农场上**

Rosenbohm的分析发现，农民主要部署通用AI工具——如ChatGPT、Google Gemini和Microsoft Copilot——多于农业专用AI工具。起草或编辑文档等办公室任务目前构成了农民使用AI的主要用途。

“在中大型农场中，我们看到AI使用已涉足商业和财务分析，”Rosenbohm说。“我们对其深入程度没有很好的了解，但他们正在试验和使用它。”

Rosenbohm说，AI有潜力将各种农业平台的数据拼合起来。

“一些调查结果显示，可能存在一些数据孤岛问题，”他说。“AI可以帮助建立连接，整合这些数据洞察。”

Schaefer指出，农业中的早期采用者将AI用于他们通常会在农场外处理的任务，例如法律或商业建议。他补充说，农民未来的一个重大机会是利用AI将产量与大宗商品市场走势相匹配。

但好处不仅限于大型农场。

“通过采用AI工具，你可以在任何规模的每个农场上推动效率提升，”Schaefer说。

**运作方式**

如果AI的使用看起来还很遥远，想想你们许多人手中的智能手机。

“如果你回到10或15年前，我们无法想象手中拥有这台超级计算机，”Farm Credit Services of America高级副总裁Jim Knuth说。“你不再需要打印纸质地图。你不必看5点新闻来了解天气。我们已经如此习惯于它的运作方式。”

Knuth看到农业中AI也在发生同样的趋势。

“我知道有些人会说，‘哦，它会毁灭世界，’”他说。“不。这不会停止。几年后，AI的使用将变得普遍，就像事物本来的运作方式一样。这将是我们推动业务所需效率的另一种方式。”
contentHtml: Large farms aren’t the only ones that will benefit from adopting artificial intelligence. AI can positively impact farms of all sizes.
